subject: HealthScope - Model fit & safety evals / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery call — model fit, evals, safety follow-ups

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for patient intake triage (symptom summarization + routing).
- Key constraints: latency target 300ms p50 per request, on-prem deployment required for PHI scope, SOC2 + BAA required.
- Data: small sample of anonymized transcripts (~3k tokens total) available for model fit tests.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Evaluation plan: run a focused model-fit sweep across two candidate families — Llama-based 13B quantized (low-cost baseline) and a tuned 70B variant (higher-quality, higher-cost). We'll run your prompt set + safety/refusal prompts and provide a per-prompt precision/recall-style breakdown.
2) Safety & guardrails: include targeted refusal prompts for suicide/self-harm, PHI extraction, and regulated-medical-advice triggers. We'll run those through our safety eval harness and return refusal/steering rates.
3) Next steps (target timeline):
   - You: confirm sample data upload to shared Drive + any additional prompt archetypes by EOD Wed (2026-06-17).
   - Us: deliver initial eval summary (metrics + sample outputs) and recommended model + quantization profile by Friday (2026-06-18).
   - Follow-up call: Wed 6/23 to review results and discuss Dedicated vs Private deployment options.

Attachments I uploaded for the eval run: healthscope_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt archetypes and expected outputs). Also linking the benchmark harness and a short eval plan in Drive.

Open items we flagged on the call:
- Confirmation from legal/procurement on BAA timeframe (Procurement team cc'd).
- Whether you prefer on-prem appliance or VPC Private deployment — we'll price both in the follow-up.

If that matches your notes I'll proceed with the eval run once you drop the sample transcripts in the Drive link below.

Thanks —

Subject: RE: Discovery call — evaluation plan & safety notes

Thanks Sarah — quick answers and plan from the SE side:

1) Medical-diagnosis prompts: our standard policy is to steer to informational responses and refuse definitive diagnoses. In the safety eval we'll run a curated set of ~120 prompts across these categories: diagnosis, triage urgency, medication advice, and PHI extraction. For each we report: response_class (refuse/steer/answer), confidence proxies, and example outputs. Expect a baseline refusal/steer rate on un-tuned 13B ~35-45% for direct diagnosis asks; tuned 70B typically shows higher-quality steering with lower false-refusal on allowed guidance.

2) Telemetry for Private/on-prem: for our Private deployment option, control plane telemetry is opt-in; customer-managed logs are default and we do not retain token-level request logs unless the customer enables diagnostic logging. We'll include a configuration doc for logging levels (none / metrics-only / diagnostic) and a sample config that ensures no token persistence.

3) Quality regression concerns: when quantizing, especially 4-bit paths, we've seen specific failure modes on longform hallucination and entity consistency. We'll include a regression check set (part of the attached eval summary) and list mitigations (small extra fine-tune, dynamic KV cache tuning, or prefer 16-bit quant profiles for critical routes).

Links and artifacts included:
- Eval harness runbook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBC-examplE-healthscope-evals
- Initial eval summary (pdf): hsc_eval_summary_20260618.pdf
- Prompt set (attached): healthscope_prompt_set_v1.json

Next steps:
- Priyom to run the first sweep on the anonymized sample once uploaded (ETA 24-48 hours).
- Marissa to coordinate procurement for BAA.

Happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk the safety prompts together.

Regards,
